newsitem.title: HONDURAS: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

HONDURAS, April 15 - Puerto Cortes - Three vessels berthed of which 2 discharging/loading containers/generals, 1 discharging fertiliser. 1 anchored in ballast. 23 Due of which 1 passenger, 11 to discharge/load containers/general, 6 to discharge/load containers/bananas, 1 to discharge generals/load lumber, 1 to load lumber, 1 each to discharge wheat/soy, coal, fuel oil.

MEXICO, April 15 - Altamira - Vessels in port, 2 general cargo, 1 repair, 1 container. Tampico - Vessels in port, 1 steel coils, 2 minerals, 1 beans, 2 general cargo. Veracruz - Port congested due to bad weather. Port closed 1400 14/4 to 0700 15/4. Vessels in port, 2 general cargo, 2 steel coils, 1 cars, 1 steel bars, 3 grain, 2 oil tankers, 3 minerals. Anchored, 2 tankers, 2 containers, 1 general cargo, 1 mineral. Manzanillo - Vessels in port, 1 cement, 2 containers, 2 general cargo, 1 clinker, 2 cars, 1 steel coils, 1 grain. Coatzacoalcos - Vessels in port, 9 tankers, 8 chemicals, 1 under repair. All ports working normally.

PANAMA, April 14 - Cristobal - 12 Vessels in port of which 6 working cargo. Balboa - 14 Vessels in port of which 1 working cargo. Panama Canal - Waterway and transit booking system normal and at full capacity. Scheduled lane outage at Miraflores locks 21/4 to 22/4 for maintenance and repairs. The test of the revised Panama Canal booking system is due to commence on 21/4. 38 Vessels due, 28 in queue, 13 booked, 37 scheduled. Further lane outages at Miraflores scheduled as follows, 2-11/6, 16-17/6, 7-19/7. Culvert outage at Pedro Miguel 11/8-1/9. Lane outage at Miraflores, Gatun 22/9-1/10, Lane outage at Miraflores 7-8/10.

UNITED STATES, April 14 - Jersey City, NJ - One vessel in port. Port Newark, NJ - Four vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Four vessels in port. Bayway, Cartaret, Nj - One vessel in each port. Honolulu, Hi - One container vessel, 4 tugs and barges alongside, 1 tanker at anchorage. Barbers Point, HI - Two barges alongside, 1 tanker in offport mooring. Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating, 7 bulkers, 4 containers, 2 ro-ro, 2 auto, 2 tankers, 3 general cargo, 3 in repair yard. 2 Bulkers awaing berth. Hampton Roads, VA - Two general cargo/container vessels in pier operating, 1 bunker in pier loading coal, 2 anchored waiting to load, 5 vessels in pier under repair and/or layberth. 1 Tanker at Sewells Point anchor lightering fuel oil, 1 bulker in pier discharging cement.

April 15 - EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - Dundalk terminal - No congestion expected this week. Clear CD canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Consol coal - Average waiting time 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities normal, no congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. New Marine terminal opened in Baltimore designed to handle breakbulk cargoes of non-ferrous metals, palletised, super sacks, forest products, project and steel cargoes. Charleston, SC - Repairs to Columbus street fender system in berths 1 and 2 will begin on Monday. However, because vessel traffic will be light, no delays are expected. No delays for cargo operations or movement is expected. Jacksonville, FL - No heavy berthing congestion or delays for the ports of Jacksonville or Fernandina Beach. Miami, FL - No congestion at the ports of Miami or Port Everglades expected this week. New York - No congestion in New York anchorages, none at container or tanker terminals. Sugar t

Norfolk, VA - Southern coal pier - 18 Vessels due during the week, no vessels anchored at present. Dominion terminal - 8 Vessels due, none anchored at present. Pier IX terminal - 5 Vessels due during the next week, 1 waiting to load. Fresh water has now been turned on for the summer at DTA coal terminal, Newport News. Norfolk southern coal pier is undergoing scheduled maintenance to the No. 1 ship loading system. Completion expected April 29. Cargill is not expecting any vessels during the coming week. Container and general cargo terminals are working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals - All working normally. All channels open, prevailing depths available. Philadelphia, PA - No port congestion in ports of Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington. No dredging/repairs/navigational problems.

Savannah, GA - Garden City terminals - Busy week expected early on, with number of ships scheduled decreasing by end of week. Ocean terminals - Look slow early on but by Thursday will be extremely busy for the remainder of the period. East Coast terminal moderate week expected, no delays expected. Colonial Marine terminals bulk clay facility - Long delays expected. Savannah sugar refinery rather slow, no delays expected. All bulk liquid facilities operating normally, no congestion expected. Navigation normal. As weather warms, afternoon thunderstorms may cause downtime on weather sensitive cargoes.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, Cargill grain elevator or Houston public grain elevator. However, congestion in some private terminals for breakbulk cargo such as Greensport terminal and Manchester terminal. Houston ship channel closed since 1020 10/4 due to a capsized deck barge. Channel expected to reopen 11/4. New Orleans, LA - Seasonal rains may cause delays in cargo operation, especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for the season. River stage at 15.8 ft. and expected to go down to 15.1 ft by 15/4. Normal transit times expected. Bar pilots advise draft for Mississippi river gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Based on these drafts, vessels advised to maintain sufficient aircraft for transit under bridges in Mississippi river. High river will cause delays in ship movement and vessel transit times. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 44 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 43 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - The Canpotex potash/sulphur loading facility commenced operation this month. Wheat vessel traffic has slowed this past week. Currently 12 grain vessels in Columbia river of which 4 loading and 7 waiting. Average waiting period 1-3 days. Coos Bay, Or - Past week normal. Glennbrook nickel dock - One vessel expected in the middle of next week. One lumber vessel loading at export services. One chip vessel expected at Roseburg dock this weekend and Roseburg dock expected to be extremely busy toward the end of this month with 4 vessels due 27-29/4. Honolulu, HI - No delays expected at offport anchorages due to weather. San Francisco, CA - Ports of Stockton and Sacramento still enforcing reduced transit draft restrictions. Maximum transit draft for vessels to and from Stockton 30 ft 06 ins. Fresh water. Vessels must arrive at the port entrance during daylight and high tide only. Dredging at Stockton continues. Controlling depth for Sacramento deep water ship channel has been changed
